body:
Fixes a regression from #6362 in `test/mpi/split_explicit_boundaries.jl`.

On `main`, `test/mpi/split_explicit_boundaries.jl` fails for one-dimensional
partitions on non-immersed grids: `u`, `v` and `η` differ between the serial
and distributed runs. Reverting #6362 makes the test pass again.

### Cause
With `ExtendedHalos`, the barotropic substep kernels run over
`surface_kernel_parameters(grid)`. This includes the wall faces and halos in the
direction that is not partitioned. There the halo keeps its original depth,
which is less than the exchange interval. So values that are out of date at the
edge of the halo move inward, and the barotropic transport at the wall faces
ends up nonzero. η is not affected, because the divergence ignores wall faces.
Before #6362, the halo fill for Ũ/Ṽ reset the wall faces through the normal-flow
boundary conditions. Since #6362 skips that fill, the transport velocities carry
flux through the walls.

### Fix
`ExtendedHalos` is selected only when there are no open boundaries and no
nonzero normal-flow boundaries, so a full halo fill is always correct in that
mode. `fill_barotropic_state_halos!` for `ExtendedHalos` now ignores
`fill_normal_flow_bcs = false`. The other halo modes, which open-boundary runs
use, are unchanged, so the #6362 fix still applies there.

### Testing
`test/mpi/split_explicit_boundaries.jl` passes on 4 GPUs (all four testsets).

### Note
This test runs only in the Buildkite distributed pipeline, which reported no
status on #6362.

title: Follow-up to #6362: refill all barotropic halos with ExtendedHalos
